I read the spec, both guidance files, the call-site inventory, every changed source file, the tests, and the three docs pages. One important process note first: **the working tree changed while I was reviewing it.** `src/cli/commands/topics-revert.ts` and `src/cli/commands/runtime.ts` both differed between my first and second reads (the first snapshot of `revertTopic` lacked the "not assigned" guard and called `forceDeleteTopic`; `runtime.ts` used `Number.parseFloat` for `--max-inline-latency`, which accepts `5garbage`). My findings below are against the **current** snapshot, which is self-consistent.

## Score: 8.7 / 10

## What is genuinely done well

- **Inventory + shared locator.** `artifacts/directional-security-profiles/implementation.json` is a real call-site inventory, and `src/airs/profile-policy.ts` is the single shared locator the spec asked for: it keeps AI-entry identity (`index`, `profile`) and `direction` attached to each protection block, marks retained legacy blocks `active: false` for directional entries (`profile-policy.ts:47`), and keeps global settings separate (`sharedProfileSettings`, `profile-policy.ts:110`).
- **Ambiguity is refused before any write.** `selectAiProfile` refuses multi-entry policies without `--ai-profile-index` (`profile-policy.ts:69`); `selectProfileProtections` refuses directional edits without `--direction` (`:89`), refuses `--direction` on a legacy profile (`:100`), and refuses unknown `content-type-mode` values in both branches (`:91`, `:104`).
- **Merge semantics.** `mergeProfilePolicy` (`profile-builder.ts:374`) extracts shared settings first, refuses >1 direction per patch, merges detectors by `name` with an explicit ambiguity throw (`:354`), and — this is the subtle part done right — validates layout on a **clone** when the protection patch is empty (`:403`), so a global-only `--direction` write does not materialize an absent direction. Tested at `directional-profile-builder.spec.ts:119`. `buildProfileOverrides` deletes `malicious-code-protection.name` (`:302`) so merges preserve the server's existing name, re-adding it only in the validation copy (`validateOverrides`, `:317`).
- **Strict directional comparison.** `runtime-policy.ts:44-51` confines every evidenced server-default allowance to non-directional entries by only rewriting the path prefix when `!isDirectionalProfile(entry)`; directional paths never match the `^model\.` patterns, so omitted-vs-present fields in a direction fail. Negative cases (action change, missing direction, dropped severity, unknown addition) are pinned at `directional-profile-builder.spec.ts:179-212`.
- **Transfer across all four directions.** `dlpReferences` and `basicFallback` iterate `profileProtectionLocations` (`runtime-profiles.ts:241`, `:268`), topic discovery stayed recursive, and the backup body still omits `dlp_tenant_id` (`:660-664`) so no tenant-bound DLP identity is transplanted. `runtime-profiles.spec.ts:712-800` covers recursive topic discovery, DLP remap, and Basic fallback in all four directions — including that `tool-response` keeps its omitted `mask-data-inline` (`:798`).
- **Reports.** `reports/runtime.ts:391-393` keeps shared latency/storage from `model-configuration` only, while `:441` summarizes every active location with `AI[n] <model-type> / <direction>`; `reports/runtime.spec.ts:356` pins that the directional fixture yields four sections rather than "no protections."
- **Release-dependency hygiene.** `package.json:64` keeps registry `0.34.0`, `pnpm-lock.yaml:170` has a registry integrity hash (no `file:`/`link:`), `prepublishOnly` (`package.json:19`) runs `scripts/check-directional-sdk.mjs`, which asserts both schemas exist *and* that they actually reject bad severities / `enable-full-conversation-inspection: "false"` / non-string `dlp_tenant_id`. The dependency is disclosed in `docs-site/docs/cli/runtime/profiles.md:75-82` and both transfer docs.
- The CLI fixture is a byte-identical copy of the SDK's sanitized fixture (verified line by line).

## Findings

**P1 — Required release work is missing.** `.changeset/` contains only `apache-license-alignment.md`. Per `CLAUDE.md` releases are cut only via `pnpm changeset version` consuming queued entries, so a user-facing feature (`--direction`, `--ai-profile-index`, directional transfer) currently has no bump entry, and `docs-site/docs/about/release-notes.md` has no directional section (its only `--direction` hit at line 637 is the unrelated DLP flag). Both are explicitly part of this repo's ship checklist.

**P1 — The reported green run does not correspond to the current tree.** The "2070 pass / 2 doc-example failures" run predates the `topics-revert.ts` and `runtime.ts` edits I observed mid-review. In the earlier snapshot, `tests/unit/cli/topics-revert.spec.ts:22-23` and `:53-66` directly contradicted the implementation. A full `pnpm test` + `lint` + `tsc --noEmit` on a frozen tree is required before this can be called verified.

**P2 — Inconsistent handling of an absent selected direction.** `selectProfileProtections` creates `content-type-configurations[direction] ??= {}` (`profile-policy.ts:97`). On `profiles update` this is harmless because the merge path clones when the patch is empty, but `assignTopicsToProfile` (`management.ts:145`) calls it on the live object, so `topics apply --direction tool-response` on a profile that has no `tool-response` block silently **creates** that direction and attaches a guardrail to it. The `profiles` path deliberately refuses to do this. Either refuse here too or require an explicit opt-in, and test it.

**P2 — Exit-code inconsistency for the same error class.** Ambiguous-direction refusal exits **2** on `profiles update` (`runtime.ts:841` → `usageError`) but **1** on `topics apply`/`revert` (`topics-apply.ts:113` → `fail`), and the new integration test encodes exit 1 at `directional-security-profiles.spec.ts:398`. Both are post-read validation refusals; pick one convention.

**P2 — Inactive legacy blocks escape the revert reference guard.** `revertTopic`'s cross-reference check (`topics-revert.ts:36`) calls `getProfileTopics(profileName)`, which filters `location.active` (`management.ts:236`). A topic still referenced in a *directional* profile's retained legacy `model-configuration` is therefore invisible to the guard: the profile PUT lands, then `deleteTopic` fails server-side, leaving a partially applied change. This is exactly the "inactive legacy protection block" class the spec calls out.

**P3 — Detector name not aligned with the evidence.** `buildAppProtection` emits `name: 'malicious-code-detection'` (`profile-builder.ts:96`), while every observed response — legacy and directional — uses `malicious-code` (fixture line 22; the allowance at `runtime-policy.ts:68` keys on `source.name === 'malicious-code'`). Pre-existing, but `--direction X --malicious-code …` now writes the unobserved name into a direction when that block doesn't yet exist. Unverified against the service.

**P3 — Empty directional create is accepted.** `buildProfileRequest` bypasses `hasAnyProtectionFlag` in the direction branch (`profile-builder.ts:247`), so `create --name X --direction response` produces `'model-configuration': {}` plus `'content-type-configurations': {response: {}}` instead of a usage error.

**P3 — Untested branches of the new safety logic.** No test covers: `getProfileTopics` returning `direction`/`aiProfileIndex` (`management.ts:249-252`); the `Ambiguous topic-guardrails identity` refusal (`management.ts:154`); `topics apply/revert --direction` against a *legacy* profile; and `canonicalPolicy`'s directional skip (`runtime-profiles.ts:562`). `tests/unit/cli/topics-apply.spec.ts` and `topics-revert.spec.ts` contain no selector cases at all — directional topic behavior rests entirely on the integration spec.

**P3 — Library surface.** `src/index.ts:13` exports only `ProfileDirection`/`ProfileSelector`. `PROFILE_DIRECTIONS`, `isDirectionalProfile`, and `profileProtectionLocations` are not exported, so library consumers cannot use the shared locator.

**P3 — Readable output.** `profiles get --output pretty` still dumps the raw policy blob (`renderer/runtime.ts:144-147`); only `dlpTenantId` was added. Directions are "included" only because the JSON is printed verbatim. The direction-aware human summary exists solely in the daily report.

## Required fixes before calling this complete

1. Add the feature changeset and the `release-notes.md` entry.
2. Freeze the tree and re-run `pnpm test`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run docs:build`, and the release checks; publish the logs.
3. Decide and test the absent-direction policy for `topics apply` (refuse, or explicit opt-in) so it matches `profiles update`.
4. Unify the exit code for post-read ambiguity refusals across `profiles` and `topics`.
5. Make the revert reference guard consider retained inactive legacy blocks (or refuse the delete when any location in the profile still references the topic).
6. Add the missing unit cases listed in P3, and either export the locator helpers or document that they are internal.

## Material limitations

- The SDK is **not published**. Tested artifact: `/tmp/airs-directional-sdk/cdot65-prisma-airs-sdk-0.34.0.tgz`, sha256 `844aec52…a947df`; I confirmed `ContentTypeConfigurationsSchema` is present in the installed `node_modules` build. Registry `0.34.0` lacks it. Clean-registry install, export verification, and `prepublishOnly` passing cannot be demonstrated until publication — correctly disclosed, and correctly gated.
- No live directional writes or cross-tenant migration. In particular, **if the service injects per-direction severity defaults the way it does for legacy `model-configuration`, directional restore read-back and `--on-conflict verify` will fail by design.** That is the spec-mandated conservative choice, but it is an untested operational risk that the docs should state in those terms, not only as "no live acceptance is claimed."
- I did not execute anything (read-only review): no test, lint, type-check, or build result here is independently verified by me.
- Private-registry audit endpoint unavailable; since `prepublishOnly` chains `pnpm audit:prod`, publish readiness is unverified on that axis too.
- The tree mutated during the review, so any file could have changed again after my last read of it.
